definition: Techniques used to prevent overfitting by discouraging overly complex models, often by penalizing large weights or adding noise.
details: Common regularization methods include L1/L2 weight penalties, dropout, data augmentation, and early stopping.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Here is the short version: Techniques used to prevent overfitting by discouraging overly complex models, often by penalizing large weights or adding noise. The part that makes it sing: Common regularization methods include L1/L2 weight penalties, dropout, data augmentation, and early stopping. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Regularization — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
